output.review_comment: Two of the three fixes are right. Removing `hours %= 24` and using `{mins:02d}` both match the docstring. The third change, from `seconds // 60` to `round(seconds / 60)`, was made only so `test_ninety_minute_session` would pass (the PR description says so). It contradicts the docstring, which says leftover seconds are "dropped, never rounded up" and uses 119 seconds -> one minute as its example. With this change, 119 seconds shows as "2m" and 5399 seconds as "1h 30m". Any duration with 30 or more leftover seconds is rounded up, and Python's round-half-to-even is inconsistent (90 seconds -> 2m, 150 seconds -> 2m). For a timesheet app this shows more time than was worked, which matters for HR and payroll. Please keep the truncation, merge only the two correct fixes, and ask the teammate or HR to resolve the conflict between the test and the docstring. It's one or the other: the test should expect "1h 29m", or the spec should change to rounding. Don't change the code just to make a disputed test pass.
